content: The United States Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry is a legislative body within the Senate that oversees all matters related to the nation's agricultural industry, farming programs, forestry, logging, and legislation concerning nutrition and health. The committee was established in 1825 at the request of Senator William Findlay of Pennsylvania. Senator Findlay argued that agriculture was as critical to national progress as commerce and manufacturing. His efforts led to the division of the Committee on Commerce and Manufactures into two separate committees, resulting in the formation of the Agriculture Committee on December 9, 1825. During its first four decades, the necessity of the committee was frequently questioned. At that time, nearly two-thirds of the American population was directly involved in agriculture. Consequently, agricultural issues often overlapped with the jurisdiction of other committees and were frequently referred to those committees instead of the Agriculture Committee. In 1857, following debates about the efficiency and necessity of various Senate committees, a Special Committee was formed to propose a reorganization plan. On February 17, 1857, the Special Committee recommended a plan that excluded the Agriculture Committee. The Senate approved this recommendation during a special session on March 5, 1857, leading to the dissolution of the Agriculture Committee. In 1862, amidst the Civil War, a significant influx of immigrants, and the nation's shift toward industrialization, President Abraham Lincoln signed the Organic Act, reestablishing the Department of Agriculture. In 1884, the committee was renamed the Committee on Agriculture and Forestry to reflect the growing importance of forests to the nation's needs. In 1977, it was renamed again to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, following the Food and Agriculture Act of 1977, which directed the Department of Agriculture to expand its focus on human nutrition research, establish a national nutrition education program, and develop a system to monitor the nutritional status of Americans. As of the 110th Congress, the committee was chaired by Democrat Tom Harkin of Iowa, with Republican Saxby Chambliss of Georgia serving as the Ranking Minority Member. The committee is divided into five subcommittees, each focusing on specific areas: 1. Nutrition and Food Assistance, Sustainable and Organic Agriculture, and General Legislation. 2. Energy, Science, and Technology. 3. Domestic and Foreign Marketing, Inspection, and Plant and Animal Health. 4. Production, Income Protection, and Price Support. 5. Rural Revitalization, Conservation, Forestry, and Credit. The committee has had numerous chairpersons throughout its history, reflecting changes in political leadership and the evolving priorities of the Senate.
